name: Méribel
description: Méribel is the central resort of the Three Valleys — literally and spiritually. It occupies the middle valley, giving it the fastest access to all three valleys (Courchevel, Belleville, and Méribel itself). Founded by British army officer Peter Lindsay in 1938 and developed with a strict wood-clad, stone-tiled chalet-style architectural policy, it is one of the more attractive purpose-built resorts in the Alps. The wooded setting distinguishes it from the treeless high-altitude resorts. A perennial favourite with British skiers.

overview.atmosphere: The heart of the Three Valleys. Chalet-architecture, British favourite, excellent intermediates terrain, wooded setting.

when_to_go.snow_reliability_note: Lower altitude base (1,450m) means snow can be thin in early December and late April. But the ski area extends to 2,950m with reliable snow above 2,000m. Méribel's wooded setting holds snow well.
when_to_go.north_facing_slopes: Good south-east aspect. Wooded slopes hold snow and provide shelter.
when_to_go.high_wind_lift_closures: Lower altitude base means valley snow can be variable at season edges

beyond_skiing.swimming_pool_or_spa: 25m indoor pool at Olympic Park with paddling pool and flume
beyond_skiing.ice_skating: Outdoor ice rink at Olympic Park, open daily winter and summer
beyond_skiing.paragliding: Tandem paragliding flights from Saulire and surrounding peaks
beyond_skiing.dog_sledding: Multiple providers — half-day and full-day husky excursions
beyond_skiing.snowshoeing: Marked trails including Plan des Mains walking paths above Mottaret
beyond_skiing.non_ski_activities: Bowling de Méribel — 6 lanes, safety barriers for children 3+, bar area, open daily. The Auditorium (310 seats, Dolby surround) + Cinema Le Mottaret
beyond_skiing.events_during_stay: Weekly events calendar: live music, farmer's market, wellness classes

best_restaurants: Le Resto (Hotel Savoy) — elegant, meat and fish, fireplace, convivial tables
La Cave des Creux — piste-side, run by locals Boris and Florian Glise, Mont Blanc views from terrace
Le Cèpe — popular, refined, charming setting, reservations essential
Le Kintessence — modern French, tasting menus
Cookie's Club — ski-in/ski-out, international dishes, sunny terrace, apres

michelin_starred.name: L'Ekrin by Laurent Azoulay
michelin_starred.cuisine: Provence meets Savoie, seasonal tasting menus

ski_area.beginners_note: Dedicated beginner zones at Méribel Centre and Mottaret. Green runs from the Olympic Park area.
ski_area.intermediates_note: Exceptional — 43% blue, 24% red. Plattières to Tougnète area is paradise for cruisers. Long red runs from top of Saulire. Best intermediates terrain in the Three Valleys.
ski_area.advanced_note: Limited blacks locally (9). Best advanced runs are off-piste or accessed via Courchevel/Val Thorens sectors.
ski_area.lift_queues: Central location means all Three Valleys traffic passes through — the main lift areas can get busy. Courchevel link especially busy.

off_piste.off_piste_detail: Excellent off-piste from Mont Vallon, Tougnète, and Saulire sectors. Powder fields above Méribel Valley. Guide recommended (Bureau des Guides).

apres_and_nightlife.nightlife_clubbing: Le Rond Point (piste-side), La Cavorite (cocktail bar), Les Enfants Terribles, Le Jack's Bar. Le Dick's Bar (iconic apres pub, live music), Le Loft (nightclub)
apres_and_nightlife.quiet_evenings: Lively but not as extreme as Val Thorens. British-heavy crowd. Pub atmosphere.

comparisons.comparison_within_domain: Less expensive, less flashy, less luxury shopping, better chalet architecture, more wooded

services.ski_hire_info: Dozens of shops — from €18/day (basic) to premium
services.supermarket_notes: Supermarket in Méribel Centre + smaller shops in each village

getting_around.parking_cost: Multiple underground car parks in Méribel Centre (paid). Free parking at resort edges.

by_train.shuttle: Frequent buses from Moûtiers to Méribel (30 min)

villages.name: Méribel Centre
villages.character: The main resort. Best restaurants and bars, Olympic Park sports complex, lively apres, central lift access. Wooded chalet-style architecture is the most attractive in the Three Valleys.
villages.dining: Le Resto (Hotel Savoy, meat/fish cuisine), La Cave des Creux (piste-side), Le Cèpe (refined), Le Kintessence

villages.name: Méribel Mottaret
villages.character: Higher satellite village. Quieter, ski-in/ski-out, closer to Val Thorens link. Good for intermediate skiers who want quick access to the Belleville valley.

villages.name: Méribel Village
villages.character: Traditional hamlet, peaceful, lower prices. Wooded setting, authentic charm. A quieter base for accessing the Méribel valley.

villages.name: Les Allues
villages.character: Original farming village at valley floor. Lower altitude, cheaper accommodation, shuttle required to reach main lifts.
villages.note: Shuttle bus to Méribel Centre lifts (10 min)

honest_drawbacks: Lower altitude base (1,450m) — snow can be thin at season edges
Central location means all Three Valleys traffic passes through — busy lift stations
Spread over 10km of valley — shuttle often required between villages
British-heavy crowd may feel less 'French' than Courchevel
Apres is good but doesn't match Val Thorens intensity
Can feel congested during school holidays
